question.leadin: Name these people who all formulated their own law codes.
question.text: This Athenian created Athens' first constitution, whose harshness gave rise to a word meaning "marked by extreme severity or cruelty."
question.clue: This man was given jurisdiction after Cylon tried to seize power, and the orator Demades joked that this man wrote in blood rather than in ink.

swap.leadin: The Phaistos Disc, an artifact found in one of this civilization's palaces, may represent an undeciphered writing system.
swap.text: Name this ancient civilization from the island of Crete, which also developed the Linear A writing system.
swap.clue: A devastating blow this civilization occurred when the Thera volcano erupted in the 16th century BCE, which contributed to their eventual decline and the occupation by the Mycenaean Greeks.

question.text: The Battle of Aegospotami ended this series of wars, which was named for a league led by Sparta. This war was temporarily ended with the Peace of Nicias [NIH-kee-as].
question.clue: The traitor Alcibiades led the ill-fated Sicilian Expedition for one side in this war that ultimately lost at the 405 BC Battle of Aegospotami.

swap.leadin: This monarch ended the tradition of the wandering Spanish Court when he selected Madrid to be the permanent capital.
swap.text: Name this King of Spain from 1556 to 1598. His faced the Dutch revolt in the Netherlands and was at one point married to England's Queen Mary I.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this name and number won the Third Sacred War against the Phocians as well as the battle of Chaeronea for Macedon.

question.leadin: The losing commander of this battle exclaimed, "my men have become women, and my women men"
question.text: Name this ancient naval battle fought in 480 BC; a major Greek victory in the Greco-Persian Wars.
question.clue: The victors at this battle had earlier suffered a defeat at Artemisium, and following this battle, the losers suffered a defeat at Mychale and another at Plataea.

swap.leadin: Following this battle, Macedonian troops captured the wife and daughters of the Persian emperor.
swap.text: Name this battle in Southern Anatolia, the second major one in the Macedonian conquest of Asia.
swap.clue: It took place after one side had reached the Beilan Pass through the Amanus Mountains, having previously captured the Cilician Gates, only to find that the enemy had snuck behind them to the Pinarus River.

question.leadin: Answer the following about numerically-named groups in ancient Greece.
question.text: This Greek historian chronicled the fighting retreat of the Ten Thousand, a Greek mercenary army in Persia, in his Anabasis. This student of Socrates also wrote a biography of Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: One of his works was an early example of the "mirrors for princes" genre, a biography entitled the Cyropaedia.

swap.leadin: The Treasury of Atreus is an example of this ancient civilization's tholoi tombs, which resemble beehives.
swap.text: Name this proto-Greek culture that was preceded by the Minoans.
swap.clue: A gate topped by two now-headless lions marks the boundary of this site's citadel and separates Grave Circles A and B at this site close to both Argos and Tiryns.

question.leadin: Plutarch reports that this man struck coins made of red-hot iron cooled in vinegar, instead of using the typical gold and silver, to reduce greed and dependence on money.
question.text: Name this legendary lawgiver who established the Great Rhetra constitution, outlined the function of the five ephors, and called for a council of twenty-eight men known as the gerousia to wield equal power to the two royal houses.
question.clue: Machiavelli and Rousseau both admired this eighth-century B.C. Spartan, who established the agoge and two kings as part of his militaristic legal reforms.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about ancient writing.
swap.text: This precursor to ancient Greek was found on records excavated at Mycenae and deciphered in the 1950s.
swap.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about artefacts made out of gold from the classical world and beyond.
question.text: A famous golden funeral mask was unearthed at the site of this older Greek civilization, and is named after the legendary king Agamemnon. This culture used the Linear B script and may have conquered the Minoan civilization.

swap.leadin: After a leader from this kingdom died, the Wars of the Diadochi saw his territory partitioned among various dynasties, including the Antigonids.
swap.text: Name this kingdom, which became dominant in Hellenistic-era Greece under its Argead dynasty. A leader from this kingdom secured victories at Issus and Gaugamela while expanding it eastwards into Asia.
swap.clue: Another ruler of it introduced the sarissa, a twenty foot pike, which allowed him to win at Crocus Field and Chaeronea before being killed by his bodyguard Pausanias.

question.text: According to Strabo, slave trading became rife on this island after the Romans captured it from Perseus of Macedon and made it a free port. Athenian executions would not take place until a sacred ship returned to this island.
question.clue: Dying in this location was prohibited in a ritual purification during the Peloponnesian War.

swap.leadin: There are three pairings in Plutarch's Parallel Lives where the Roman's section comes before the Greek's.
swap.text: Timoleon is paired with Aemilius Paullus, who won the battle of Pydna after his maniples outmaneuvered this dynasty's pikemen. This dynasty was founded by a general nicknamed "One-Eyed."

question.leadin: Name some things related to Greek historians who wrote about Rome.
question.text: This 2nd century Greek author was a political prisoner in Rome where he tutored Scipio Aemilianus and chronicled the rise of Rome in his Histories, which contain an important description of Hannibal's invasion of Italy.
question.clue: After that, he became a tutor to the sons of the general Lucius Aemilius Paulus, including Scipio Africanus, whom he followed to witness the destruction of Carthage.

swap.leadin: Antigonus I died during this battle, which was won by Lysimachus and Seleucus I.
swap.text: Name this 301 BCE battle fought in Phrygia by members of the Diadochi. This battle stopped Antigonus from reuniting the lands of an earlier ruler.
swap.clue: The deciding maneuver in this battle was the separation of the loser's cavalry from their main force by Seleucus' elephants.

question.leadin: Although Pausanias of Orestis was responsible for this event, it remains unclear if he acted alone or was part of a conspiracy.
question.text: Describe this event which took place at the wedding of Alexander I of Epirus in the historic capital Aegae.
question.answerHtml: assassination of Philip II of Macedon [or death of Philip II; accept synonyms for assassination; prompt on Philip; prompt on partial answers]
question.answer: assassination of Philip II of Macedon
question.clue: By some accounts, Alexander is implicated in this 336 BCE event, which victimized the creator of the sarissa spear. This event, which occurred at Cleopatra's wedding, was perpetrated by the victim's lover, Pausanias.

swap.text: Troops from this city were the only ones to help Athens at the Battle of Marathon. According to Herodotus, Aristides ("air-ih-STY-deez") the Just led Athenian forces at a battle near this city that was honored with the "Serpent Column."
swap.clue: This city's strategic position came from its overlooking the road from Thebes to Corinth.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Leonidas' predecessor Cleomenes I.
question.text: Cleomenes I waged war against this other city and defeated it at the Battle of Sepeia in 494 BC. This city earlier defeated Sparta at Hysiae, during which it was ruled by Pheidon.
question.clue: Weights and measures found at the Heraion of this city are said to date to the reign of King Pheidon, who ruled this city as a tyrant.

swap.text: This Spartan, a daughter of Archidamus II, is apparently the first woman to win at the Olympics, having won two chariot races. "Winning" in that case meant owning and training the chariot team, as women were strictly banned from even watching the games.
